correctness.rationale: For arbitrary finite group G and iid law mu, output words have |G| lifts per lag-residue chain; exact finite entropy follows. Infinite past and future each identify the boundary initial letters modulo the left-translation stabilizer by iid empirical frequency reconstruction. Both observed halves are independent conditional on the recoverable coset vector, giving I=k(H(mu)-log2|Kmu|). Stabilizer closedness and explicit distinct-coset law perturbations prove the precise cluster-set and continuity classification, including laws with zeros and nonnormal subgroups. 38 independent brute-force finite word comparisons succeeded; experiments do not replace infinite proof.

value.rationale: The group-difference factor is a natural symbolic observable. The full subgroup-stabilizer invariant makes past-future information an exactly classifiable parameter-singular quantity, with quantized intermediate jumps and nonnormal examples absent in the classical binary case. Every stabilizer can occur for a strictly positive source law, so the classification gives a structural phase diagram rather than isolated arithmetic instances or a binary renaming.
